beats.text: Ask an AI to fix a broken form, and it will tell you it's fixed. The page loads. A confirmation appears. But did the user's booking actually get saved, correctly?
Here, the booking page says success. But the database stored the wrong phone number. Nobody notices, unless you check what was saved.

AccessFinish drives the journey in a real browser, then hands the evidence and the source code to NVIDIA Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory. No hints. Nemotron finds the hard-coded value, and writes the fix.
beats.say: AccessFinish drives the journey in a real browser, then hands the evidence and the source code to NVIDIA Nemo-tron, on Nebius Token Factory. No hints. Nemo-tron finds the hard-coded value, and writes the fix.

beats.text: Every fix is built in a fresh, offline sandbox, and checked for real: the saved database row, a fresh browser, and a second customer with a different number. Seven live runs. Seven verified fixes, on the first attempt, for about half a cent each.
Now the harder case. A keyboard user can't reach the date picker at all.
Nemotron reads the source files, proposes fixes, and every attempt is built and tested. It makes the date reachable, and the page says the booking is confirmed.
beats.say: Nemo-tron reads the source files, proposes fixes, and every attempt is built and tested. It makes the date reachable, and the page says the booking is confirmed.

beats.text: But AccessFinish reads the database. The booking was saved for the wrong day. Rejected.
And it shows exactly why. Seven tenths of a second after a background request, with no key pressed, the date resets itself to the first of the month.
Fifteen fake booked confirmations, across seven runs. Not one got through.
Fourteen live runs, and forty-one cents of Nemotron. Fixes that are proven, not promised.
beats.say: Fourteen live runs, and forty-one cents of Nemo-tron. Fixes that are proven, not promised.

beats.text: AccessFinish. Finish the task. Verify the result.
